reviews.title: Less Intuitive With Every Update
reviews.text:
I’ve been a paying subscriber for nearly two years, largely because I meticulously track my workouts and didn’t want to lose my training history.

I won’t be renewing.

What originally attracted me to Boostcamp was its clean, intuitive design. Over time, the app has become increasingly cluttered with programming I don’t use, and features that were once easy to access have been buried behind additional taps.

A perfect example is workout history. There used to be a simple calendar view that made it easy to see every day you trained and quickly review your consistency month by month. Now that view is tucked away, making something I used regularly harder to find for no apparent benefit.

The exercise library is also more limited than it should be, with many common variations missing. 

I’ve stayed this long because my workout history is valuable to me, but the user experience has steadily declined. Moving years of training data to a new platform will be a hassle, but at this point it’s worth it.

If you value simple design, intuitive navigation, and quick access to your workout history, there are much better and cheaper options out there.

reviews.title: Used to be good. Now it’s far from.
reviews.text:
This app used to be much better, and I’m not talking about UI choices. I’m seriously considering switching apps at this point, but I feel locked in because all my old workout history is stored here. The behavior has really gone downhill recently (vibe coded?), e.g.

The workout progress on the lock screen rarely shows up anymore. This used to be essential for me timing my rest.

Data does not sync between the web and mobile versions well, losing data. I’m completely fed up with this because I wasted near an hour today trying to edit a program, and then opening it in the app reverted everything I did.

The program creator is buggy because it combines sets of the same number of reps, so you cannot edit them on the web version; the editor shows different numbers than the viewer. It will also have the wrong number of sets listed at times, and it loses the sets and reps suggested for exercise alternatives.

Certain custom exercises do not show up in exercise search some days. I cannot notice a pattern in this.

Some exercises are duplicate if you create a custom exercise with the same name as one that is later officially added to the app.

There are way too many buttons to press to add a note to exercises during a workout. Why is it fewer buttons to swap exercises than it is to add a quick note to what I did?

reviews.title: Did a test year, think I’m done
reviews.text: The App is nice and fun to track. But not necessary. Over time it has declined in performance.  Tracking has been finicky, numbers logged during the week don’t show up on end of the week summaries, and sometimes your PRs don’t show up at all.  Additionally, some exercises that are programmed in, do not populate in the list of exercises that you can choose from to either add or substitute for another exercise on a different day.  Like, where did the exercise go?  I’m a believer in getting what you paid for and when performance declines, you’re not. On top of that where as before, the App Store showed that they reported no data is tracked or linked to you, now that is not the case.  I was doing just fine prior to the app and will after this subscription dies.

reviews.title: Great gym app, but price is far too high given alternatives
reviews.text:
Love this gym app, been a user on multiple accounts since they posted on /r/nsuns

£14.99 is just far too much for a gym app and the features don't justify it given the alternatives apps around that offer similar, at this point I am sticking to the app just because i'm used to it

To put it into perspective, spotify and Netflix subscriptions are actually cheaper than a gym app

However amazing app, great features, and they absolutely do listen to the community, just seems in recent years they have been realising the potential income and have been systematically moving free features behind paywalls and spamming free users with upgrade information

The free version id genuinely give a 1star, even clunky apps like jefit or strong offer better free options if you take the time to get through their clunky interface

The paid version id genuinely give 5 star, if it were more reasonably priced, in comparison to other apps you would be better off paying less, i'm only remaining subscribed for ease of use while I recover from a motorbike accident as I enjoy the great interface and custom exercise features

Great app, but in brutal honesty, for £14 there are better alternatives, the free version is not worth it if you are serious about working out, £8.99 seems a more reasonable price for an app of this type
